title: NFL trade deadline buyers and sellers: Dallas Cowboys, Chicago Bears, LA Chargers, Arizona Cardinals - CBS Sports
description: As the sixth week of the NFL season arrives, the gap between Super Bowl contenders and teams vying for favorable positions in the draft
body:
As the sixth week of the NFL season arrives, the gap between Super Bowl contenders and teams vying for favorable positions in the draft has begun to grow. Once teams recognize their spot in the pecking order, they can chart their path forward for the rest of 2026 and beyond, and one of the first decisions to make is whether to buy or sell at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. That mark is already less than a month out, so there are only a few games left to help front offices decide whether to add impact talent or ship it out in exchange for draft capital.A few teams have already begun this process. On Sunday, the Arizona Cardinals traded wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans in a move that padded the former's draft coffers and gave the latter a high-upside depth piece on offense who could get his career back on track in a new situation. Before Harrison, Cam Jurgens, Joey Porter Jr. and J.J. McCarthy hit the trade block.The question is not whether there will be a flurry of moves at the deadline — that is a given. It is more about which teams will make them. Once it becomes clear who is buying and who is selling, the players involved will, in many cases, be quite obvious.
Here are the teams that could buy and sell at the deadline and the players that may be on the move.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seller: ChargersSell candidates: Khalil Mack, Donte Jackson, Quentin Johnston, David NjokuWhy wait until the deadline to move on from obvious trade candidates such as Mack? The Chargers are, shockingly, going nowhere fast at 0-5 and face a grueling schedule between now and Nov. 10, so they may as well get out ahead of the market and sell before they lose even more leverage. This roster and its coaching staff might have simply run its course, because after years of coming up short in the postseason, their chances of even getting back there in 2026 are bleak at best.Mack is by far the most tradeable player on the roster as a 35-year-old playing extremely well on a one-year contract. That is the exact kind of rental player that defense-needy playoff contenders are in search of every single year. 
Teams with holes on the back end of the defense could call about Jackson and his expiring contract, too. He racked up nine interceptions across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, after all. And on the other side of the ball, someone will look past Johnston's drop problems and see his physical attributes as worthy of investment. Meanwhile, Njoku should be a cheap option at tight end.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buyer: BearsBuy candidates: Khalil Mack, Josh Sweat, Daron Payne, Zach SielerSo long as Ben Johnson is around, the Bears will not have trouble putting points on the board. Once Caleb Williams returns to the lineup, Chicago will be back in the mix for prime positioning in the NFC playoff hunt, and it already showed it can stay afloat for however much longer he is on the sideline. In order to maximize the team's upside upon Williams' return, general manager Ryan Poles needs to bolster the defense, especially up front. The Bears rank just 20th in quarterback pressure rate and lack depth on both the edge and interior.What about a reunion with Mack? He spent four years of his prime with the Bears and clearly still has something to give with three sacks in five games this season. Perhaps they could acquire Sweat instead. They have just enough cap space to bring him in this year before his salary balloons in the final two years of his contract. The edge rusher spot should be a higher priority than defensive tackle since the Bears were mostly quiet at that position in the offseason and just saw Marcus Davenport abruptly retire after Week 4.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seller: TitansSell candidates: Tony Pollard, Calvin Ridley, Jermaine Johnson IIIf a Titans breakthrough comes during the Robert Saleh era, it does not appear it will happen in Year 1. This franchise is still stuck in rebuild mode and needs to acquire as much draft capital as possible to round out its core of Cam Ward and Carnell Tate with more young prospects. That means cutting bait on what already looks like a lost season, parting with the tradeable veterans, hoping that Ward shows signs of improvement in the second half of the year and making good use of what should be another early first-round pick in 2027.Pollard is among the biggest names across the NFL who could be next in line to be traded. The former Pro Bowler is on an expiring contract and perhaps in the final stages of his prime. He would be a terrific No. 2 option for a team that already has a standout starting running back. Ridley already seems to be in the midst of his decline and is no longer a regular starter, but was a perennial 1,000-yard receiver as recently as two years ago. And even though the Titans traded for Johnson in the offseason, they did so knowing he would play 2026 on his fifth-year option and could flip him in an attempt to get something in return rather than watching him leave at the end of his contract.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buyer: CowboysBuy candidates: Maxx Crosby, Alex Highsmith, Khalil Mack, Josh SweatJerry Jones is in a trading mood already and made a splash when he acquired Joey Porter Jr. The defense still needs help, though. After they added Porter, the Cowboys could shift their focus back toward the front of the unit and continue to address the edge rusher spot, which has been a weakness ever since they shipped Micah Parsons out of town. Jones has not been shy about wanting to shore up the defense through the trade market and is always one for the marquee transaction, so Dallas might not be done big-game hunting.
        
            
                Cowboys' Jerry Jones expresses interest in making trades despite embarrassing loss to Buccaneers
                
                    Garrett Podell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
By the time the deadline arrives, the Cowboys might have just enough cap space to add Crosby to their payroll. They reportedly made three offers to the Raiders prior to the nixed deal that would have sent him to the Ravens, so it does not take much imagination to picture them making another push. The bigger question is whether Las Vegas still has any interest in moving him. Dallas could also look back to Pittsburgh and try for Highsmith, who could be the odd man out in a three-person pass-rushing system that also features T.J. Watt and Nick Herbig. The Cowboys already pulled off three trades with the Steelers over the last year and a half, so there is a fruitful working relationship between the two front offices.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seller: DolphinsSell candidates: Austin Jackson, Zach Sieler, Josh UcheTo climb out of the deepest rebuild in the NFL, the Dolphins have to establish a core around which they can build a roster. There are early signs of one existing in standout first-year linebacker Jacob Rodriguez and rookie wide receivers Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell, but Miami needs another big draft like the 13-pick haul it put together this past spring. While it lacks a volume of tradeable veterans and will have a hard time receiving Day 1 or Day 2 capital in return, there are a couple who could help the Dolphins pile up selections in the later rounds.Jackson is off to a rough start as the 71st-rated offensive tackle among 72 qualifiers, per PFF, but tackles are always in demand. He would be an affordable half-season rental. Sieler, at 31, is much older than the defensive pieces the Dolphins plan to build around. Uche is the strongest candidate of the three to re-sign with Miami, but even that is no guarantee.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buyer: 49ersBuy candidates: Jerry Jeudy, Khalil Mack, Josh Uche, Daron Payne, Zach SielerThe 49ers own the best resume in the NFL with wins over the entire rest of the NFC West, plus the Broncos and Dolphins. They played better over five games than any other Super Bowl hopeful, but with a roster loaded with older and oft-injured players, their ability to stay in the hunt is always tenuous. 
San Francisco can never have enough weapons. In order to keep this train rolling, general manager John Lynch should add startable depth at the deadline to prevent any catastrophic drop-offs should injuries further plague his team down the stretch and into the playoffs. He has all the room on his payroll he needs to do so with $41.9 million in salary cap space, which is the most of any team, per Over The Cap.The wide receiver position was hit hardest by the rash of early-season injuries. The passing attack remains elite with quarterback Brock Purdy playing the best football of his career and Mike Evans doing what he always does as the No. 1 target. But the depth issues stemming from Ricky Pearsall's season-ending injury and the ailments of De'Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel emphasize the need for more bodies. Browns receiver Jerry Jeudy might be there for the taking, judging by how he has been phased out in favor of a couple of standout rookies. And that's just one option.Defensively, the 49ers surprisingly stood mostly still in the offseason, so there remains a necessity for more depth up front. Mykel Williams' return in Week 5 from a torn ACL could be enough to keep them from making a splash in this group, though.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seller: BuccaneersSell candidates: Chris Godwin, Kenneth Gainwell, YaYa Diaby, A'Shawn Robinson, Zyon McCollumThey finally got up off the mat with a "Thursday Night Football" upset of the Cowboys, but this remains a concerning start to the year for the Buccaneers as coach Todd Bowles seeks to hang onto his job. If that win proves to be a blip on the radar, Bowles will become even more of a lame-duck coach, and the front office could begin a teardown of the roster. In that event, there are a number of assets who would become obvious trade bait.The biggest question mark among the potential movers is McCollum, who is in the midst of a rebound season after he signed a three-year contract extension in 2025. Would his strong individual start to the year halt the Buccaneers from lumping him in with the more no-doubt trade pieces like Gainwell and Robinson? Or would they commit to a full rebuild and attempt to sell high on a player who could garner a more impactful return package than he would have at this time last year?

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buyer: LionsBuy candidates: Zyon McCollum, Donte Jackson, Greg Newsome II, Kristian FultonThe Lions will go as far as the offense carries them. That is, unless they address one of the NFL's most glaring needs: help in the Detroit secondary. While Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown will keep them in essentially every game they play, they cannot keep surrendering at least 21 points in each outing as they did in Weeks 1-5 if they are to make the playoffs. Losing Terrion Arnold in the offseason continues to prove mighty costly, especially given that both starting safeties from a year ago, Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, are on the shelf with injuries.Detroit would stand to benefit from a potential fire sale in Tampa Bay, because that would probably make McCollum available for the right price. There are several directions the Lions could go at cornerback, and they can afford to be aggressive. They own the second-most cap space of any team with $33.9 million available, and as a team that has to strike now to maximize its contention window, any and all draft picks should be on the table.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seller: CardinalsSell candidates: Josh Sweat, Budda Baker, Gardner MinshewWith one in-season trade already complete, the Cardinals have established themselves as sellers. Other teams will likely call to see just how many players they are willing to part with, as the team seems destined for a last-place finish in the NFC West and is liquidating pieces that do not fit into first-year coach Mike LaFleur's system.
Sweat is the clearest candidate to leave, given the offseason buzz that suggested he wanted out of Arizona. He dispelled that narrative, as did general manager Monti Ossenfort, but perhaps there is fire behind the smoke. The former Pro Bowler may return the best trade package of anyone the Cardinals would realistically move.Baker also ought to command early-round picks given his status as a perennial Pro Bowl honoree and the fact that he will remain under contract through 2027. And with the potential for the Cardinals to activate Carson Beck as their backup quarterback, the likelihood of them keeping Minshew around as a No. 3 option decreases.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buyer: RaidersBuy candidates: Brian Thomas Jr., Jerry Jeudy, Quentin Johnston, Calvin RidleyFirst-year coach Klint Kubiak has the Raiders surprisingly ahead of schedule and could keep them in the postseason hunt deep. A team that once seemed poised to sell at the deadline and continue drafting around Fernando Mendoza might actually be a buyer. If Las Vegas does go after anyone, it would most likely target a wide receiver to add to a group that lacks a bona fide No. 1 target and is young with a low ceiling. Once Mendoza eventually steps into the starting lineup, the Raiders will want to have plenty of reliable receivers there to help him settle in.If anyone makes a bet on Thomas rekindling his rookie-year magic, the Raiders are a logical choice to do so. Thomas is still only in his third year of pro football, so if he were to right the ship, he would fit ideally with the rest of Las Vegas' nucleus of Mendoza, Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty as recent arrivals in the league. If they cannot obtain him or the Jaguars hesitate to sell, the Raiders should have plenty of other options, albeit with less upside.

title: Why Victor Wembanyama is poised to level up in Year 4 takeover -- and possibly join historic MVP/DPOY company - CBS Sports
description: Wemby, ranked CBS Sports' No. 1 NBA player, is still growing, even after asserting himself as the best in the gam
body:
Wemby, ranked CBS Sports' No. 1 NBA player, is still growing, even after asserting himself as the best in the game
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When Victor Wembanyama came into the NBA as the No. 1 pick in 2023, the hype, quite literally, couldn't have been any bigger. Wait, you're telling me there's a 19-year-old kid in France who makes seven-footers look small with the skills of a guard? Yes, that's what we're telling you. You can imagine the "OK, buddy" snickers, because honestly, if you weren't tapping into the EuroLeague circuit, the idea of this guy sounded inconceivable. Some freakish combination of Kevin Durant and Bill Russell? What are you going to tell me next, that in his third NBA season, he's going to become the first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year in league history, finish third in MVP voting and go to the Finals, where his team will hold the lead for more than 70% of the total minutes played, by way of a Game 7 road win over the defending champion Thunder? Funny you should ask. As it turns out, that's precisely what Wembanyama accomplished last season despite not being old enough to legally buy a beer until the month before the All-Star break. His learning curve looks like the vapor trail of a rocket ship headed straight for the moon. Not since LeBron James, who averaged an astonishing 31 points, seven rebounds and six assists in his third NBA season, has a player been this dominant this soon. When LeBron carried the 2007 Cavaliers to the Finals, he was 23 days younger than Wemby was when he made his Finals debut on June 3 against New York. LeBron is arguably the greatest player in NBA history, which is probably the only career outcome that could have actually exceeded the teenage expectations with which he was saddled.

        
            
                Ranking the NBA's top 100 players: Victor Wembanyama enters 2026-27 season at No. 1
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
It's close to the same for Wembanyama, who is already on a GOAT trajectory. Everyone knows you're supposed to wait until a player has won at least one championship and/or MVP, or hell, at least until he's actually through his rookie contract, before you even start whispering things like that, but Wembanyama is leaving us no choice. He's the best defensive player on the planet to the degree that Stephen Curry is the best shooter on the planet. Just about everything else in basketball is debatable. Those two things are not. Both Curry and Wembanyama warp the geometry of a court in ways nobody could have imagined before they came along. Curry stretches defenses. Wembanyama shrinks offenses. NBA.com tracking defines an "open" shot as the nearest defender being at least four feet away, but tell that to all the scared-to-death scorers who have been forced to rewire every spatial instinct they've spent a lifetime calculating, parading into the paint only to come running right back out as if they've seen, well, an alien. 
On one half of the court alone, Wembanyama is among the most impactful players in the game. The fact that last season, he became the only player in history to average at least 25 points, 11 rebounds and three blocks on 62% true shooting was enough to claim the No. 1 spot on our CBS Sports Top 100 player rankings. Quibble with that designation if you must. Call it premature. Maybe it is. There are no fewer than five players with a reasonable claim to that throne, one of whom, Jalen Brunson, just bested Wembanyama in the Finals. This is a projection for what's ahead, however, and the fact of the matter is Wembanyama -- who clocked in at 5-foot-7 in the second grade and hit 6-5 before his 13th birthday -- is growing too fast for anyone to keep up with for much longer. Wemby's next stepThis is what's most exciting. We get to watch these growth spurts happen in real time, from season to season, month to month, sometimes even game to game. In the first playoff game of his career, Wembanyama hung 35 on the Blazers. When the Timberwolves had the Spurs 2-2 in the second round after Wemby was ejected early in Game 4, he fired back with 27 points, 17 rebounds, five assists and three blocks as San Antonio won the next two games by 59 points. 
Then it was OKC in the conference finals, where the dream season was supposed to finally end. Until Wemby went for 41 points and 24 boards in a double-overtime Game 1 win, that is. For me, and I suspect a lot of others, this was the night Wembanyama became the best player in the world. So far, this is the signature shot of his career. 
The nerve to even take that shot as a dead-tired 21-year-old playing in your first conference finals game is one thing. The ability to actually make it as a 7-foot-4 center is out of this world. These are Steph Curry shots, plain and simple. This crossover-into-stepback 3 in a preseason game last week should be impossible for a man of Wembanyama's size. Shots like this are almost too accessible for Wemby at times. He can get them whenever he wants, and they're a hell of a lot of fun to take, but the reality is that he was only a 34% 3-point shooter last year. He doesn't overdo it (five and a half 3-point attempts a game feels about right for now), and the threat of it alters spatial dynamics in ways traditional shooting percentages can't encapsulate, but on any given night, Wemby can be susceptible to falling a bit too deeply in love with the deep ones. 
Indeed, the most obvious next step in Wembanyama's offensive evolution is continuing to drill down on the right shots from the right spots. At the moment, he doesn't have a quote-unquote office. No kill zone like Kevin Durant at the elbow, Carmelo Anthony facing up or SGA stepping back. He may never have such a specific go-to spot or shot given his fluid, freelancing ways, but in general, he can stand to more consistently establish himself closer to the basket. That's easier said than done. Part of it is just having the intent to do so, but the sheer strength to do it is another matter. Wemby is still maturing physically. Isaiah Hartenstein manhandled him at times in the conference finals -- literally pushing him out of the paint as Wemby was forced to initiate almost all his offense for long stretches from the perimeter, particularly in Games 2 and 3 after he was so dominant in the paint in the series opener. It was largely the same story early in the Finals, when the Knicks forced him to take 22 of his first 42 shots from outside the paint. But each game, he forced his way a little lower on the court, and by Game 3, you could see the clear markings of his efficiency growing as his average shot distance shrank. 
Game 1: 17.3 feet -- 33.3 eFG% Game 2: 13.2 feet -- 57.1 eFG% Game 3: 10.6 feet -- 66.7 eFG%None of this is to suggest that Wembanyama shouldn't look to utilize his jump shooting abilities, but this also isn't rocket science. The closer that a guy who can touch the rim without his feet leaving the ground can operate to the basket, the better. This can happen in a variety of ways. Rim rolls. Short rolls. Post-ups. Lobs. Dunker's spot catches. Face-ups from the Joel Embiid free-throw-extended zones, where he can put the ball on the floor and reach the rim in a single step.As defenses collectively sink to deter Wemby's point-blank finishes, the soft spots in the short mid-range -- where he took just 20% of his shots last season and made just 42% of them, per Cleaning the Glass -- are seemingly ripe for growth with more frequent exploitation. This preseason look Wemby got against the Suns is a prime example. Not all jumpers are created equal, and again, 3-pointers, self-created or off the catch, are going to and should be a part of Wemby's arsenal, but on some level, every 3-point shot that Wembanyama takes, especially the crazy off-the-dribble ones, is a win for the defense. 
The next step is about launching as many offensive attacks as possible on his terms. Understanding that he is still figuring out what those terms are is going to be like watching a young dinosaur slowly realizing its power to destroy everything in front of him. Predictions for Year 4MVP and DPOY: The 65-game rule will be interesting. The Spurs have the depth, both top end and overall, to deploy Wemby with greater caution as they balance the long- and short-term goals of his career. At the same time, Wembanyama has been open about his accolade ambitions. Wemby wants the MVP, and my guess is he gets his first one this year along with his second straight unanimous DPOY. This will make Wembanyama just the fourth player in history to win both awards in the same year, joining Michael Jordan, Hakeem Olajuwon and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Spurs win it all: I'll take it one step further and say that Wembanyama becomes just the second player to add a championship to that ledger in the same season, as only Olajuwon has done. It won't be easy. The Thunder were missing Jalen Williams and Ajay Mitchell for the most part when the Spurs eliminated them last season, and the Knicks dominated them in crunch time. But the Spurs are too much. Wemby has a spell over Chet Holmgren, and the fact that San Antonio has him, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper all still playing on rookie contracts allows them to keep De'Aaron Fox's $229 million contract on the books as a luxury third guard, at least until they potentially trade him for even more talent. Either way, there is an embarrassment of riches piling up in South Texas.

        It may be partially the product of having four teams on a bye, or all the injuries at the wide receiver position, but one thing you'll notice when looking at this week's Fantasy Football wide receiver rankings is that good things come in twos. In our consensus rankings, there are two Cowboys in the top 12, but we always expected CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to be that good. It's also not surprising to see Puka Nacua and Davante Adams in the top 16, especially when you consider they are playing the Cardinals. But what about two Packers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, in the top 14? Or two Panthers, Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker, in the top 18? Or two Saints, Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, in the top 24? That's right, 10 of our top 24 receivers this week come from five teams. That's shocking. What's more shocking is that the Steelers almost made it six.Even after his disappointing Week 5, DK Metcalf comes in at WR21 in our consensus rankings and he is ranked top 25 in all three experts' rankings. You might think that's because Michael Pittman and Roman Wilson are out, but if you scroll down just a bit further, you see the top waiver wire receiver, Germie Bernard, ranked at WR27. What in the world?Bernard did catch six of nine targets for 80 yards in Week 5, so this isn't coming out of nowhere. But how can we be so confident in two receivers for Aaron Rodgers? Credit Mike McCarthy. Rodgers is averaging 36.8 passes per game and eight air yards per attempt. His 65.5% true dropback rate is his highest in the last five years and more of those targets are going to receivers than they did last year. Rodgers isn't his old self, not by any stretch, but the combination of volume and downfield targets has made his receivers more viable than they've been in a while. title: Why it's time for rookie Carson Beck to replace Jacoby Brissett as Cardinals QB - CBS Sports
description: A look at the Cardinals' quarterback outlook and when Carson Beck should start
body:
A look at the Cardinals' quarterback outlook and when Carson Beck should start
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Arizona Cardinals (1-4) have hit their ceiling with Jacoby Brissett as their starting quarterback in 2026. Since defeating the now 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, Arizona has lost four in a row, including a damning couple of losses the last two weeks. The Cardinals had a chance to beat the New York Giants in Week 4 with a play at the 4-yard line, trailing by six with 11 seconds remaining. After using their final timeout, Brissett threw a pick-six, the third of his single-game career-high three interceptions that day. Equally — or perhaps more — damning is what happened on Sunday in Arizona's 45-21 defeat against the Detroit Lions. The Lions entered Week 5 with the league's 31st-ranked scoring defense (31.8 points per game) and the NFL's worst total defense (423.8 total yards per game) and third down defense (52.8% third down conversion rate allowed). After an opening drive touchdown pass from Brissett to tight end Teagan Quitoriano, the Cardinals' next five drives were three-and-outs. That's right. Arizona had five consecutive three-and-outs against the league's worst total and third-down defense. Their next drive ended with an interception. It wasn't until the game was essentially over that Brissett found the end zone again.That leaves the question: Is it time for Carson Beck to take over in Arizona?A closer look at BrissettEvery quarterback who had played the Lions entering Week 5 stuffed the stat sheet and either beat Detroit or lost to them by one possession. The Brissett-led Cardinals losing to the 2026 Lions defense, which is missing both All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph and Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch, by 24 points is unacceptable. 
Quarterbacks vs. the Lions this seasonNew Orleans Saints' Tyler Shough (Week 1): 35-for-56 for 410 yards passing, three passing touchdowns, two interceptions in a 31-30 OT lossBuffalo Bills' Josh Allen (Week 2): 20-for-31 for 248 yards passing, three passing touchdowns; 14 carries for 69 yards, two rushing touchdowns in a 41-31 winNew York Jets' Geno Smith (Week 3): 31-for-37 for 321 yards passing, three passing touchdowns in a 31-24 lossCarolina Panthers' Bryce Young (Week 4): 29-for-41 for 329 yards passing, two passing touchdowns in a 32-26 win 
Brissett's production this season — 66.3% completion percentage, 1,110 yards passing, nine passing touchdowns and five interceptions for an 85.2 passer rating — isn't terrible, but it's all empty calories in that it mostly happens with the game's outcome no longer up in the air. The 2026 season isn't an outlier for Brissett either. In 2025, he threw for 3,366 passing yards, the second most in the NFL since becoming a starter in Week 6, but they weren't impactful. Arizona won just one of Brissett's 11 starts in 2025, and it was against the Dallas Cowboys, who owned that season's worst scoring defense (30.1 points allowed per game). Brissett is what he is: a 33-year-old journeyman on his sixth NFL team in 11 seasons who is limited as a full-time starting quarterback. Should it be rookie Carson Beck's time?A strong case could be made that 2026 third-round pick Carson Beck should begin to receive increased reps in practice before eventually replacing Brissett in the starting lineup. Beck played just one preseason game, the Hall of Fame game against the Carolina Panthers, but he performed well. He threw for 188 yards and a touchdown while completing 15 of his 19 throws. 
A rib injury cut short his development opportunities as he missed the final three Cardinals preseason games. Thus far this season, he has been the emergency third quarterback on game day. "If we think that's what's best," said Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur on Monday when asked about moving Beck to an active role. "We haven't had those discussions. We'll end up having that discussion [Tuesday]."   Sure, a one-game preseason sample size isn't incredibly indicative of a quarterback's long-term NFL potential, but it's worth ramping Beck up to start. The next two weeks are against difficult defenses in the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos, but Arizona should target Week 8 for Beck to make his regular-season debut. 
Why Week 8? That's when the Cardinals will head to AT&T Stadium to face the Dallas Cowboys (2-3), the only team Brissett beat in 2025 and the owners of the NFL's current seventh-worst scoring defense (27.2 points per game allowed in 2026). The Cowboys are fresh off an embarrassing loss to the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who earned their first win of 2026 with undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels making his second career start.Arizona needs to get Beck, an older rookie who will turn 25 years old in November, reps for at least the second half of this season. It'll only help to assess what the Cardinals have in him ahead of utilizing another high draft pick in the vaunted 2027 NFL Draft. If they like what they see, the Cardinals can simply go with the "best player available" approach. If they don't, they may need to take a longer look at the upcoming quarterback draft class.

title: Will Chargers trade Justin Herbert? Update on possibility of QB being dealt, possible landing spots - CBS Sports
description: Herbert's name has started to circulate ahead of the NFL's trade deadline
body:
Herbert's name has started to circulate ahead of the NFL's trade deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the Nov. 4 trade deadline rapidly approaching, rumors and rumblings have intensified regarding potential players who may be on the move. One of those players is Justin Herbert, the Chargers' embattled quarterback who has played some of the worst football of his career through the season's first five games. His struggles have coincided with the Chargers' dreadful 0-5 start to the season. Despite Herbert's struggles this season, the Chargers would be well-compensated if they decided to trade him. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter said that a high-level executive threw out a hypothetical scenario to him where the Chargers traded Herbert for three first-round picks. Intrigued, Schefter then reached out to the Chargers to see if they would actually consider trading Herbert. "The person basically cut me off mid-sentence," Schefter said. "Stopped me in my tracks and said, 'Let me be very clear about this. We have never even discussed that idea. The sentence -- should we trade Justin Herbert -- has never once been uttered in our organization, nor will it be.'" Based on that report, it appears that the odds of Herbert being traded are about as good as Herbert winning league MVP this season. Despite their current predicament, the Chargers apparently still believe that Herbert is their long-term franchise quarterback and is capable of playing high-level football again. 
That may be true, but teams often have a change of heart. Nothing can entirely be ruled out in sports, especially in the NFL, where things seem to change on a dime. That's why, even if it is unlikely, the prospect of Herbert being traded can't be dismissed entirely, especially when you consider what the Chargers would get for him. In that vein, here are several teams that would likely be in play if Herbert were made available for trade: 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsThe Vikings were the first team to come to mind. Despite their 5-0 start, Minnesota's offense remains bogged down by middling quarterback play. 
While that is true, it's hard to imagine the Vikings doing anything dramatic unless the team goes into a funk sometime between now and the trade deadline. Kyler Murray, for all his faults, is 4-0 as Minnesota's starting quarterback. It's worth repeating, however, that the Vikings could decide to pull the trigger on something of this magnitude if the offense continues to lag behind the defense. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York JetsIf the Jets want any chance of being relevant by season's end, they need to do something drastic on the offensive side of the ball. Trading for Herbert would qualify as such. 
Gang Green's defense is currently fifth in the NFL in fewest points allowed. The offense, however, is among the league's worst in several areas, most notably in points scored. With 10 picks in the upcoming NFL Draft, the Jets have the resources to make a splash at the deadline. That makes this scenario even more likely if the Chargers have a change of heart with Herbert. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tennessee TitansIt would be hard to blame the Titans if they chose to end the Cam Ward era after less than two years. Ward hasn't made significant strides this season, and it's one of the reasons why the Titans are 0-5. 
While he wouldn't change their fortunes that much this year, Herbert would infuse some optimism into a fan base that badly needs it. The Titans could certainly use more optimism as they prepare to open a new stadium in 2027. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Miami can get a do-over after drafting Tua Tagovailoa instead of Herbert in 2020. Miami DolphinsThe Dolphins are in the first year of Malik Willis' contract, but anyone who has watched Miami knows that Willis isn't the team's long-term solution at quarterback. Instead of riding it out with Willis, the Dolphins would be better served finding a better option at the most important position in sports. 
More so, Herbert's arrival would give Miami's long-suffering fanbase some much-needed hope. The Dolphins, after all, haven't had a quarterback of Herbert's caliber since Dan Marino, who retired at the end of the 1999 season. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Philadelphia EaglesAs unlikely as this scenario is, it makes a lot of sense for both franchises. Both Herbert and Jalen Hurts could use a change of scenery. Herbert has regressed in Los Angeles, and the same can be said of Hurts in Philadelphia. For the Eagles, Herbert could potentially jumpstart their playoff hopes if Philadelphia can find a way to win some games ahead of the trade deadline. Hurts, in turn, would be a better fit in Mike McDaniel's offense.

title: Texas Tech football: What's wrong with the Red Raiders despite a 5-0 start? - CBS Sports
description: A regressing secondary and Will Hammond's turnover troubles have the Red Raiders searching for answers despite a
body:
A regressing secondary and Will Hammond's turnover troubles have the Red Raiders searching for answers despite a second straight 5-0 start
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        No. 10 Texas Tech was a heavy favorite to win the Big 12 for the second straight season after cruising to the College Football Playoff last year. Through five weeks, though, returns have been decidedly mixed. The Red Raiders rank outside of the top 10 of the Big 12 in both offense and defense. They're 12th in yards per play and are tied for worst in the conference with six interceptions. Their only ranked matchup at home came down to a stopped two-point conversion against Houston. Texas Tech is sitting at 5-0 in consecutive seasons for the first time in program history. These are champagne problems for a program that has rarely contended for conference championships across its history. "Do I want to be more explosive on offense? Do we want to be more efficient on offense? One hundred percent," McGuire said. "And we have to find ways to do that. But I'm going to take the win every time." 
But after winning the Big 12 and recording the program's first AP Top 10 finish in history, more is expected. What's gone wrong in Lubbock? Diminished defenseLast season, Texas Tech absolutely nailed its star-studded transfer class. David Bailey, Romello Height and Lee Hunter were All-America candidates along the defensive line. Tight end Terrance Carter Jr. and cornerback Brice Pollock were elite level performers. It was a once in a lifetime series of hits for the recruiting staff in Lubbock. But while they swung for the fences again, replicating the hit rate was no easy feat. 
Through the first five weeks, Texas Tech ranks a stunning No. 73 in total defense and ninth in the Big 12 in yards per play defense. The secondary has gotten picked on consistently to the tune of the No. 127 passing defense, a miserable start. After finishing No. in sacks last season, the Red Raiders are at No. 69, projected to nearly half their mark from last season. There's plenty of blame to go around, but the underwhelming defensive line transfers stand tall. None of superstar transfers Adam Trick, Mateen Ibirogba or Trey White have recorded more than one sack. Jamond Mathis has 2.5, but they all came against Abilene Christian. The linebackers continue to be a strength of the team, especially returners Ben Roberts and John Curry, but transfer Austin Romaine hasn't lived up to expectations outside of a couple of pick-sixes against Sam Houston. Texas Tech wanted to build its identity as a hard-nosed defensive team under Joey McGuire, but the unit is underperforming and putting more pressure on the offense. Replicating last year's No. 3 total defense was never realistic, but the collapse has been notable. 
Hammond's inconsistencyTexas Tech invested a significant amount of money in the transfer portal to land five-star quarterback Brendan Sorsby. While the staff had faith in sophomore Will Hammond, the Hutto native was coming off a torn ACL last October, and the staff wanted insurance. Through five games, Hammond looks the part of a talented quarterback still adjusting after an offseason away from football. Hammond has thrown a touchdown in every game and completed 68% of his passes, but also has five touchdowns to five interceptions as he questions his eyes. Three of the picks came in a sequence against lowly Sam Houston. Hammond has shown several flashes over the course of two years. Against Utah last season, he came off the bench for an injured Behren Morton and helped lead a massive second-half run to win 34-10. This year against Houston, Hammond stepped up with the best game of his career, shaking off an early interception to throw for 257 yards and a touchdown in a win. 
His tentative nature has appeared in the numbers. In four of his games, Hammond's passes have hovered around a middling eight yards per attempt. Against Houston, when the program's back was against the wall, Hammond delivered 11.6 yards per attempt. The offensive line has been disappointing through the first couple of weeks, and the running game has not delivered despite three talented running backs. But ultimately, Hammond has to create gravity with the passing game to give the offense a chance to find its footing. Time to growTexas Tech received fair criticism for a middling nonconference schedule, which makes their overall schedule one of the easiest among contenders. At the time, No. 22 Houston was the only ranked team on their schedule, though Oklahoma State has risen to No. 18 and Arizona is flirting with a national ranking. 
Oregon State set off some alarm bells when they challenged the Red Raiders in a 35-24 game, but that win is aging better. The Beavers are up to No. 37 in the CBS 138 and have two certified superstars in quarterback Braden Atkinson and wide receiver Jesse Legree. Both of their losses are to ranked Big 12 teams. Following a bye, Texas Tech plays Arizona State and, on the road, a hostile Cincinnati squad in the coming weeks. Then it's home games against Arizona and West Virginia before the road trip to Stillwater, which could be the most difficult game of the year. The schedule allows the Red Raiders to grow while remaining in contention for the Big 12 title game. But unless improvement comes, Texas Tech could quickly find itself on the outside looking in.

title: Brian Flores-NFL lawsuit: Recruiting firm memo filled with racial stereotypes, attorneys claim - CBS Sports
description: Flores, Steve Wilks and Ray Horton have an ongoing lawsuit against the NFL for racial discrimination
body:
Flores, Steve Wilks and Ray Horton have an ongoing lawsuit against the NFL for racial discrimination
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the latest development in the Brian Flores lawsuit against the NFL for racial discrimination, a recruiting firm memo regarding Flores possessed examples of what his legal team labeled as racial stereotypes and talking points teams use in reference to potential Black head coach hires. A memo put together for the Las Vegas Raiders by the recruiter Korn Ferry during a recent head-coaching search became unsealed in court on Tuesday. It is part of the lawsuit from Flores — and former head coaches Steve Wilks and Ray Horton —against the league and six teams. Front Office Sports obtained and published a copy of the memo on Tuesday. In the report, it was noted that he was "polished and a good presenter" despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn, the same area as notorious heavyweight champion boxer Mike Tyson. Flores' lawyers argue the report assumes someone from the predominantly Black area of New York wouldn't have strong public speaking skills. According to the NYU Furman Center, just over two-thirds of Brownsville's population, 67.6%, is Black. "Polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson)," the memo read, via Front Office Sports. "He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire's son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals." 
Flores' attorney, Michael Willemin, told Front Office Sports that the write-up paints Flores as an "angry Black man." Willemin pointed to the "polish upwards" reference in his "Weaknesses" section as a racial stereotype that downplays Flores' intelligence as a minority. Other "Weaknesses" comments his lawyers point to in the report read:He can fool you with his polish upwards. Has little people skills, lacks self-awareness and can sometimes exhibit erratic behavior. Tua's [Tagovailoa's] statements have opened the narrative that Brian was "pessimistic and adversarial" and his style "shattered his confidence."Wants to be a CEO-type Head Coach but micro-manages in a negative manner. Makes knee-jerk reactionary decisions based on the last play.Chip on his shoulder — can be a dictator with players, coaches, and can even be difficult with ownership. His personality is unpredictable — not sure who is going to show up. Failed in how he hires coordinators and staff because he doesn't give second chances or see efforts to improve.Needs someone strong at the top to reign [sic] in some of his worst behavior. He once threatened violence to his GM and made irrational demands during an ownership meeting. One long-time senior team executive said, "He may have changed since, but he was the worst hiring decision we've ever made." Another President of a club refused to talk about him."Flores, who has been the Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator since 2023, following three seasons as the Miami Dolphins head coach (2019 to 2021), has the Vikings out to a 5-0 start in 2026. Their undefeated record is largely on the strength of his complex blitzing, disguise coverage scheme. Minnesota has the fewest touchdowns (9) during a 5-0 start since the 2003 Carolina Panthers, while Flores' defense ranks first in the NFL in scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) in 2026. Flores' unit also leads the league in quarterback pressure rate (46.4%), sack rate (9.8%), blitz rate (69.8%), completion percentage allowed (53.2%) and passer rating allowed (62.9). 
Flores first sued the NFL in 2022 and was later joined by Wilks and Horton. The Tua Tagovailoa comments referenced in the report refer to when the ex-Dolphins quarterback labeled his former head coach as "a terrible person" in 2024. Tagovailoa, who is now the back-up quarterback with the Atlanta Falcons, said Flores shook his confidence that he could be an NFL quarterback.The current Vikings defensive coordinator responded to Tagovailoa's comments in August 2024, and he said he used that feedback to grow as a leader. "Look, I'm human," Flores said at the time, specifically when asked about Tagovailoa's "terrible person" depiction. "So that hit me in a way that wasn't ... positive for me. But at the same time, I've got to use that and say, 'Hey, how can I grow from that? How can I be better?' And that's really where I'm at from that standpoint. Do I feel like that's me? No. But how can I grow from that situation and create a world where that's not the case that anyone says that about Brian Flores?"

title: Who won the James Franklin-Penn State breakup? One year later, there are no winners - CBS Sports
description: When Penn State decided to fire James Franklin on Oct. 12, 2025, it did so to send a message. After three straight losses to Big Ten opp
body:
When Penn State decided to fire James Franklin on Oct. 12, 2025, it did so to send a message. After three straight losses to Big Ten opponents, a Nittany Lions squad that was seemingly set up for success had underperformed to the point that athletic director Pat Kraft wanted to step in and steer the football program in a new direction. It was an emotional decision to part ways with a coach in Franklin who had led Penn State to 104 wins and five top-10 finishes across a 12-year tenure. But Kraft, in his press conference explaining the firing, said the move had to be made immediately in the best interest of the players on the team and the direction of the season. At the time, Penn State was 3-3 on the year. One year later, the breakup between Penn State and James Franklin has sent both parties on a wild ride, with each side, at different times, feeling they were indeed better off after the split. But the cruel twist of this particular week, the one-year anniversary, is that it finds both Penn State and James Franklin in eerily similar states of disappointment, with a lot of work left to do to make the best of their first year in a new situation in 2026. James Franklin was fired, Matt Campbell was hired, and millions were spent on the coaching change, yet Penn State found itself with a 3-3 record again on Oct. 12. 
So let's detail the chapters of the last year for this breakup, noting specifically when each side has seemingly had an argument for "winning" the split and ultimately the path ahead for both Penn State and Franklin. While this week paints a particularly bleak picture (they are currently a combined 0-4 against teams with a winning record), there are plenty of opportunities to flush the past and rewrite the present. 
        
            
                Penn State fired James Franklin to join college football's elite -- instead, it became a cautionary tale
                
                    John Talty                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Chapter 1: James Franklin feels the love while Penn State searches for partners James Franklin was a little bit surprised by Penn State's decision to move on six games into the season, but it also made him an early "home run" candidate for Virginia Tech as the Hokies fired Brent Pry even earlier in the 2025 campaign. Franklin had about $49 million worth of reasons to remain out of coaching, but a full-court press from Virginia Tech, including a plan for enhanced investments and the opportunity to get back to work, brought him to the table. After a settlement with Penn State and a new contract was secured, Franklin received a hero's welcome in Blacksburg as the kind of coach who can return the Hokies to the top of the ACC. He got Frank Beamer's blessing for the job; he retained his former assistant, Brent Pry, as defensive coordinator and quickly began assembling a staff of former colleagues to work on his plan for the 2026 season. In just about five weeks' time (from getting fired on Oct. 12 to being hired on Nov. 17), James Franklin had gone from being blindsided by a firing to feeling an outpouring of love and support at his new school. 
Meanwhile, Penn State was left playing the waiting game. While Franklin was officially out of work for just 36 days, Penn State endured a 54-day coaching search to replace him, leaving Nittany Lions fans with a very different feeling. Because while Franklin quickly picked himself up, found a new home and hit the ground running (which included efforts on the recruiting trail that impacted Penn State), athletic director Pat Kraft was working his way through in-season due diligence on potential candidates. If Penn State was going to hire a sitting head coach, then it wasn't likely to happen before the end of November, but it seemed savvy at the time to be one of the first brand names open in what was expected to be a busy coaching carousel. One by one, more big-time schools joined the coaching carousel. And much to the displeasure of Penn State fans, those jobs were also filled before the Nittany Lions had introduced their new head coach. Making matters even more frustrating was seeing some of the potential big-name candidates come off the board due to new contract extensions. Indiana coach Curt Cignetti dispelled any rumors or reports quickly with a new deal announced by the school on Oct. 16. Matt Rhule played at Penn State and worked at Temple with Pat Kraft, but he agreed to a new contract extension with Nebraska on Oct. 30. Texas A&M coach Mike Elko also landed a new deal on Nov. 15, and after that things started to quiet on the Penn State coaching front. When word got out that Kalani Sitake had become the focus of Penn State's search, BYU activated its community -- from Crumbl cookies to reworked investment strategies -- to ensure the Cougars wouldn't lose one of their own. 
By the time Iowa State coach Matt Campbell was hired in early December, Penn State could feel satisfied with the result even if the process was exhausting. Campbell's reported interest or non-interest in the job had been miscommunicated at some point in the process, but that didn't undo the angst of watching a handful of SEC jobs both open and get filled in the time it took to make the hire. James Franklin spent those 54 days getting wooed, celebrated and feeling the love. By the end of 54 days at Penn State, they were happy to have a qualified candidate say "yes."James Franklin was introduced as Virginia Tech coach on Nov. 19, 2025, a little more than a month after Penn State fired him. 
                                                                    Imagn Images
                                                            Chapter 2: Talking season sharpens expectations Though James Franklin and Matt Campbell have different personalities, they both command the podium with presence and carry themselves with obvious confidence in media days-type settings. And sure enough, both the Penn State and Virginia Tech fan bases came out of the July-August preseason run-up with an idea of what they were going ot get in Year 1 with a new head coach. The expectations were different for both personnel and scheduling reasons, but they were mostly clear. And for Penn State, those expectations are making the current struggles even more disappointing.  Matt Campbell brought with him not just two dozen former Iowa State players but also a handful of assistant coaches and support staff to help lay the foundation of his program in State College. The players discussed this in the preseason, heartwarmingly telling tales of the large group chats where Penn State holdovers could offer advice on places to go around town, while the Iowa State-infusion crowd could help the rest of the team understand what makes their new coaches tick. This roster transition seemed to be going much more smoothly than the coaching search, so even if Penn State was replacing eight NFL Draft picks, it appeared to be a group that could contend in the Big Ten. 
Many experts liked the Penn State roster Matt Campbell put together, but they really loved the schedule. After James Franklin spent most of his career with annual games against some of the best teams in the Big Ten, Penn State entered 2026 with a slate that avoided the preseason favorites. With no games scheduled against Indiana, Ohio State or Oregon, the Nittany Lions had seemingly avoided the toughest foes and stood a chance of being favored to win in as many as 10 games. Penn State wasn't going to be compared to Indiana or Ohio State in a power ratings-style discussion, but finding a way into the College Football Playoff picture (even as a contender) was in the cards if it could win some of the coin flips against teams like USC and Michigan. We had not even seen a down of Penn State football under Matt Campbell, but "Penn State CFP dark horse" was already on the lips of the more optimistic Nittany Lions fans. Meanwhile, on the Virginia Tech side, the schedule was a sobering piece of the preseason conversation. It might have actually freed James Franklin up to drive home his enthusiasm for the roster he had assembled, including former Penn State standouts like quarterback Ethan Grunkmyer and tight end Luke Reynolds, and the emotion of unlocking enthusiasm in a college football hotbed like Blacksburg. But with games against Miami, SMU, Clemson and Virginia, the Hokies were staring down three of the four teams that have played in the ACC Championship in the last two years, as well as last year's national runner-up. If Penn State felt like it had fallen behind in the break-up battle with James Franklin back in December, the summertime preseason leveled the playing field with more optimism for on-field success.  
Rocco Becht, one of the most experienced quarterbacks in college football, followed Matt Campbell from Iowa State to Penn State this offseason. 
                                                                    Imagn Images
                                                            Chapter 3: Penn State, Franklin both enjoy success On the afternoon of Sept. 5, hope truly was springing eternal for both Penn State and James Franklin. The Nittany Lions were in total control, and new starting quarterback Rocco Becht was showcasing how this Iowa State infusion could lead to wins in Happy Valley. Becht threw for four touchdowns and 271 yards in a 45-0 win against Marshall, which only even crossed midfield three times the entire afternoon. What followed was a somewhat sloppy win at Temple, then an apparent course correction against Buffalo, with the team rising to No. 13 in the rankings on the back of a 3-0 non-conference record. Three wins against three lesser opponents masked some of the uncertainties or unknowns about the roster, and certainly kept any Penn State fans from wondering if history was about to repeat itself heading into Big Ten play. In Blacksburg, things were equally optimistic for James Franklin as Metallica rang out from the speakers in Lane Stadium and the Hokies raced out a 4-0 start to the season. Virginia Tech thrashed VMI and Old Dominion, then turned Maryland into turtle soup with a strong second half in College Park. The quality of performance dipped a bit in one of the many rain-slogged affairs of this 2026 season, but emerging from Chesnut Hill with a win against Boston College provided the Hokies a stage to make some national noise heading into October. In terms of the breakup, this is where friends of both Penn State and James Franklin would celebrate how both parties have found happiness with their new partner. Penn State redecorated a little bit to match its new head coach, and Franklin was revitalized by the opportunity to bring Frank Beamer's program back into national prominence. If Franklin got the leg up early, and Penn State caught up in the preseason, here we see both of our subjects flying high, unaware of the despair that's to come in the next couple of weeks.

        
            
                Getting the band back together: James Franklin, Brent Pry and Virginia Tech's strange do-over
                
                    Brandon Marcello                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Chapter 4: Mistakes compound into season-defining disappointmentsA 3-yard touchdown run by Rocco Becht gave Penn State a 17-0 lead against Wisconsin early in the second quarter at home early Saturday evening on Sept. 26. That is, according to our analysis, the last point of pure optimism that Penn State has experienced this season. All the Nittany Lions had to do was outplay Wisconsin for the rest of the way, and they would improve to 4-0 and potentially start to enter the conversation as a top-10 team. Instead, defensive breakdowns and empty possessions on offense allowed the Badgers to overcome that 17-point deficit and storm back to win 24-20. Then, on a short week, the Penn State defense got exposed for its deficiencies against the run as Northwestern rolled up 413 rushing yards in a 34-13 blowout win to open new Ryan Field. In two weeks, the Nittany Lions had gone from potential top-10 team to playing a secondary character in Chip Kelly's biopic and struggling to get stops in ways that could get exposed against other Big Ten opponents. Then came last week's White Out, with an opponent in USC that has struggled on the East Coast and a home fan base that did not want to watch a second loss of the season. The game was much closer and more competitive than the loss to Northwestern, but Penn State failed to score a single touchdown in the second half and lost 31-23. 
It was a loss that left Penn State at 3-3 on the year and 0-3 in Big Ten play, matching the records the Nittany Lions had when they fired James Franklin. The painful twists and turns of this breakup did in fact reach Franklin's door as well. Virginia Tech had a 14-0 first-quarter lead at home against Pittsburgh in a battle of ACC unbeatens that was sure to send one team into the top 25. But the Hokies gave the game away with four turnovers and 82 penalty yards, finding themselves trailing 35-33 despite out-gaining Pitt 499-295 for the game. John Love's 36-yard game-winning attempt hooked left, but was close enough to being good that even Love thought he had made the kick. It was just a few inches off line, but the mistakes that preceded the kick were worth much more than that. Things got worse the following week as Virginia Tech traveled out to Berkeley to play California, and even though the Bears were without starting quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, the Hokes struggled to take control of the game. There were five lead changes in total, but the last was the most painful, as Virginia Tech's defense allowed Cal to march right down the field in the final minutes for a game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds left on the clock. A few inches away from being 5-0 turned into 4-2 quickly, and the heart-breaking nature of both defeats will wear on Hokie fans when they reflect on the season.   
Early-season optimism has evaporated for first-year Penn State coach Matt Campbell on the heels of three straight losses. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Chapters TBD: The path forward  While we have chosen this one-year anniversary to recap the ups and downs of the post-breakup lives of both Penn State and James Franklin, it's important to note that the story is far from done. Moments like Friday, Oct. 2 when both Penn State and James Franklin are losing at the same time in gut-punch fashions (with different margins) make it seem like these two are tied together forever, but we know that is not reality. Penn State and James Franklin each have six games left to put a stamp on their Year 1 in a new relationship, and that's plenty of time to undo the mirroring despair that we've seen in recent weeks. For Penn State, that starts with Saturday's trip to Ann Arbor against a Michigan team facing its own existential crisis post-new hire. It's an opportunity against a historic rival that could turn a season around, much like how Oklahoma flipped negative vibes with a win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry. A win would not indicate that all issues are solved, but it would make things feel less bleak. James Franklin now has his own turnaround moment as well, with Virginia Tech playing host to Georgia Tech in Blacksburg. It's a tough turnaround from losing in Berkeley to being back in an ACC game seven days later, especially against a Yellow Jackets team that's surging after upsetting Duke. One year after Penn State fired James Franklin, it's easy to wonder whether either is better off in this moment. It's possible we still think that at the end of the year, but what this moment, heading into Week 7, presents is far more urgency for success than what either might have imagined at the start of the year. After all, moving on and moving out of this cloud of disappointment has to start with the first step, and the first step is snapping their respective losing streaks.

body:
From Dan Quinn heating up his hot seat in Washington to Jim Harbaugh owning up to a fourth-quarter collapse in Los Angeles, we rank the week's most brutal sideline decisions
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Week 5 in the NFL featured some pretty incredible coaching gaffes that directly led to losses. Whether the leaders in charge of their teams just zoned out for a second, forgot what situation they were in or chose the wrong strategy, multiple fan bases were driven to madness by their franchises' decision-makers.There were coaches who forgot about the clock, coaches who got either too aggressive or too conservative, and a coach already on the hot seat who admitted he cost his team the game. Week 5 almost saw it all when it comes to coaching blunders. Below, we break down and rank the notable coaching gaffes from this past week in the NFL, going from "That's pretty egregious," to "Sir, what the hell are you doing?"4. Jim Harbaugh"I can't think of a time I've ever been more mad at myself"
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            The 2026 season has been a nightmare for the Los Angeles Chargers. Not only are they 0-5, but the Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel marriage has not gone according to plan. Plus, injuries are again beginning to mount.
It looked like the Chargers were on their way to winning their first game of the season against the rival Denver Broncos on Sunday. The Chargers held a 17-10 lead early in the fourth quarter and just watched Wil Lutz miss a 42-yard field goal. They had all the momentum, but Jim Harbaugh wanted more. The Chargers decided to go for it on a fourth-and-1 at their own 41-yard line. Herbert was stuffed, and the Broncos took over on downs. That fourth-and-1 failure marked the beginning of the end for Los Angeles. The Broncos went 41 yards on five plays and tied the game with a Courtland Sutton touchdown. Then, two plays into the Chargers' next possession, Herbert was sacked and fumbled away the ball. That turnover led to a Broncos field goal, which gave Denver a 20-17 lead. On the Chargers' next possession, Herbert threw an interception on fourth-and-6, setting up another Broncos field goal. Denver won, 23-17. 
"Yeah, it was the wrong decision, I've never — I can't think of a time I've ever been more mad at myself," Harbaugh said after the game.
Harbaugh is in the midst of his first eight-game losing streak if we include last season's playoffs. It's the longest losing streak of his career as a head coach in the NCAA or NFL.3. Sean McVay"It's been a while since I've been this pissed after a game"
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            The Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams on Monday night was a potential Super Bowl preview, and this game required a fifth quarter to determine a winner. Both teams scored touchdowns in the final two minutes to get the game to overtime, and the drama continued in the extra period. 
The Rams won the overtime coin toss and elected to kick since both teams now receive a chance to possess the ball in the extra quarter. It looked like the Bills were well on their way to a touchdown to open overtime, but then James Cook III fumbled at the Rams' 22-yard line. It was recovered by Aaron Donald, and Matthew Stafford took over, needing just a field goal to win. The Rams quickly got into enemy territory thanks to a 21-yard pickup from Puka Nacua. It was at the Bills' 35-yard line where Sean McVay began to feel comfortable. On second-and-10, he called for a short pass to Nacua, which picked up five yards. On third-and-5, he called a Kyren Williams run that got stuffed at the line of scrimmage. That set up a 48-yard Harrison Mevis field goal attempt for the win. If "48-yard field goal attempt from Mevis" sounds familiar, it's because he missed a 48-yard field goal just last week against the Philadelphia Eagles. He also missed a 50-yard field goal in the first quarter on Monday. Now, a 48-yard field goal is definitely makeable, but certainly not a gimme. Sure enough, this potential game-winning kick was tipped by Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau. The Bills then went 35 yards down the field and kicked a game-winning 45-yard field goal to hand the Rams a 37-34 loss.
McVay's conservative play-calling and decision to go for a 48-yard field goal with his struggling special teams was mind-boggling. Consider that the Rams had registered THREE STRAIGHT touchdown drives to end the fourth quarter. That includes a possession where L.A. went 63 yards down the field on eight plays with 1:30 remaining in regulation to send the game to overtime. Now, with the game on the line, McVay is choosing Mevis over the reigning NFL MVP?!"It's been a while since I've been this pissed after a game," McVay said in his fiery postgame press conference.
As CBS Sports' Zach Pereles pointed out, the Rams rank dead last in special teams EPA this season:
The Rams are 5-for-9 on field goals this year, the worst rate in the NFLThe Rams are 29th in yards per kickoff return and 26th in yards per kickoff return allowedThe Rams are 30th in net yards per punt and 26th in opponent net yards per puntMcVay really trusted this unit over the TOP OFFENSE IN THE NFL. The Rams are now 2-3 because McVay played it too safe.2. Nick Sirianni"I lost us that game"
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            No one expected it, but the Eagles' Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London ended up being one of the best games of the week. It looked like the Eagles had registered a massive upset victory at the end of the fourth quarter, but jubilation turned to depression in the span of eight seconds. With 1:35 remaining in the fourth quarter, down 16-14, Jalen Hurts led his offense 32 yards downfield on nine plays, setting Jake Elliott up for a 48-yard field goal. He nailed it, putting the Eagles up, 17-16, with eight seconds left on the clock. 
On the kickoff, the Eagles elected to kick the ball in play instead of kicking it into/out of the end zone, allowing Ameer Abdullah an opportunity to make a play. And make a play he did. Abdullah broke loose for 53 yards to set Jaguars kicker Cam Little up with a game-winning 57-yard field goal. 
Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni accepted blame for the decision to put the kickoff in play and for the devastating loss as a whole. "I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that's what I said to our guys, and what hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game," Sirianni said. "I put that fully on me."
So, why did Sirianni leave the ball in play? One could assume the Eagles wanted to allow a few of the eight seconds to run off the clock as the Jaguars returned the kickoff. The one thing you can't do is allow the returner to break loose, which is what Philly did. The 2-3 Eagles are now under .500 for the first time since 2021. Sunday's loss snapped a franchise-record streak of 76 games where the Eagles were .500 or better, per CBS Sports Research.1. Dan Quinn"That's my responsibility, nobody else's"
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Without a doubt, the worst gaffe of the week — and maybe of the season — goes to Dan Quinn of the Washington Commanders. This is the kind of mistake where you may never look at your head coach the same again. It may be the first thing people point to when Quinn is eventually fired, because it was a sequence that warmed up his seat that much more.The Commanders and New York Giants went to overtime in a rain-soaked Northwest Stadium with the score tied at 27 apiece. Giants kicker Dominic Zvada missed a 46-yard field goal to begin the extra period, while Washington was forced to punt after picking up just one first down. The Giants then took over with 5:33 remaining in overtime and needed just a field goal to win. Jameis Winston got New York down to the Washington 24-yard line, but Cam Skattebo fumbled the ball. It was recovered by Shy Tuttle, and the Commanders stole possession with 1:55 left on the clock and zero timeouts remaining. Remember that key detail. 
Washington put together three chunk plays to get into field goal territory with one minute left in overtime, and that's when everything went awry. The Commanders rushed Rachaad White for two yards and watched as the clock wound down under 30 seconds. Quarterback Jayden Daniels snapped the ball with about 13 seconds remaining, danced around, and then took a dive for a loss of one yard with eight seconds left. The clock continued to run, and the Commanders could not get back to the line to spike the ball. They ran the clock out on themselves, leading to a 27-27 tie.
Coach Quinn threw his headset down and stood on the sideline in disbelief. Obviously, the head coach deserves blame — no one on the field was aware of what to do in a critical situation. We aren't even sure if the players knew they had zero timeouts remaining. It's the head coach's responsibility to control the operation, manage the game and have everyone on the same page. Quinn did none of that on Sunday, leading to one of the worst mistakes we've seen in the NFL. 
While Quinn rightfully deserves blame for what happened at the end of this game, he's not the only one I have a problem with. David Blough's play call: Did you notice on Washington's last play, the offense used a motion man? Daniels motioned tight end Ben Sinnott back and forth as the clock went from 16 seconds to 13 seconds. That's absolutely hysterical. What purpose could a man in a motion serve in that situation when the ticking seconds are precious? It's fair to speculate that if Daniels hadn't used a motion man, the Commanders could have gotten off the spike and kicked the game-winning field goal! That's a first-year offensive coordinator for ya. Jayden Daniels' lack of football IQ: I don't care if the head coach is paying attention or not, as a quarterback, you have to be aware of the situation and the clock. Daniels saw the clock at 13 seconds when he snapped the ball. At that point, you're throwing it away to the sideline or throwing it in the dirt. You're not taking a sack. No starting quarterback should have to be told that. No urgency from other players: It really felt like most of the Commanders on the field were not aware they had zero timeouts. When Daniels took his dive, no one was rushing to the line of scrimmage to spike the ball. You shouldn't have to explain this situation to professional football players, but apparently Quinn needed to. 
However you want to spin it, this mistake is on Quinn for not having his team ready for an end-of-game scenario, and the Commanders missed out on a win because of it.

One interesting feature is Flex payouts. As users add more legs to their entries, they get higher payout multipliers. However, depending on the number of legs, it is possible for a user to still get paid out with one or more incorrect picks.  If any leg has a Tie/Void ruling, it just becomes an entry with one fewer leg. For example, if a user has a five-leg entry and one leg is a tie/void, Underdog will now follow a payout structure for a four-leg entry.  Underdog also has a concept called Rivals within Pick Em, which pits two players against one another in a statistical category with an adjustment for one player. What to expect from the former EuroLeague point guard and how it affects St. John's outlook in 2026-27
